narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is a settled interior condition - to lie down and sleep in peace - and the type (D102) confirms it is a state, not an act or a plot: the inner being is being described in its resting posture, not caught doing anything. The bearer (D105) is the psalmist himself (inferred), and the operation (D106) traces the whole movement: the self lies down and sleeps in peace, God alone making it dwell in safety - rest as the fruit of trust. The target (D107) is that peaceful-rest, and the coupling (D112) welds sleep to safety, so the interior state and the security that grounds it are a single knot. The absences read as evidence: source (D103, present:false) is unstated because this rest has no interior cause upstream of itself - it does not arise from an emotion or an organ but simply is what trust settles into; seat (D104) is explicitly 'none', so the peace is not lodged in a bodily organ but pervades the whole self; manner (D108) is 'none', for the lying-down needs no qualifying style; intensity (D109), specifier (D110) and effect (D111) are all present:false - the state is not measured, not narrowed, and produces no further downstream effect because it is itself the terminus. Prohibition (D113) is absent: nothing is forbidden here, this is a state permitted and enjoyed. The discovery note (D114) reads the evening as the mirror of Psalm 3's morning: sleep is the body's confession of security in God. Role (D115) is characteristic and locus (D116) is internal:ib-state - a genuine inner-being condition. Within the deceit-falsehood family this is the pole opposite to lies: the interior that rests undefended is the interior that has no falsehood to guard.
narratives.story: Here the inner life is caught at rest: a person lying down and falling asleep in peace, kept safe through the night by God alone. Nothing is being done or plotted - this is simply what a trusting heart settles into when the day ends. The peace is not tucked away in one corner of the body; it fills the whole person, and it needs no explanation, no special effort, no measuring. There is nothing forbidden here and nothing left over - the rest is the end of the road, the body's own quiet confession that it feels secure. It is the exact opposite of a lying, anxious heart: the one who has no deceit to hide is the one who can sleep undefended.

narratives.narrative: This is slander read in the negative - the sense (D101) is 'refuses to slander', and the type (D102) is volition, so the finding is not an act of deceit but a deliberate act of the will that declines it. The bearer (D105) is the righteous (inferred), the one qualified to dwell on God's holy hill. The operation (D106) lays out the whole movement: he does not slander with his tongue, does no evil to a neighbour, takes up no reproach against a friend - restrained speech that protects others. The target (D107) is tongue-restraint, and the coupling (D112) is 'no-slander', so the governed tongue and the withheld defamation are one interior discipline. The absences are telling: source (D103, present:false) - the restraint has no named upstream cause because it flows from the integrity of the whole man (v2, 'speaks truth in his heart'), not from a discrete impulse; seat (D104) is 'none', so this control is not seated in a single organ but is the temper of the person; manner (D108) is 'none'; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) all present:false - the refusal is not graded or narrowed, and no downstream consequence is recorded because the point is the standing character, not its outcome. Prohibition (D113) is absent as a recorded flag even though the content is a self-imposed prohibition - the negation lives in the sense and operation, not as a separate divine ban. The discovery note (D114) fixes the operation as the governed tongue: the interior refuses to trade in others' reputations. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. In this family it is the reverse image of the slanderer and the lying tongue elsewhere: the inner being that will not weaponise speech.
narratives.story: This time the trait appears as something a person deliberately will not do. The one fit to live close to God is the one who chooses not to run others down - he keeps no cruel word behind his teeth, does no harm to a neighbour, will not pick up a rumour against a friend. The restraint does not come from some single feeling or from one part of him; it is simply the grain of an honest man whose whole heart already speaks the truth. It is not measured or partial, and the passage does not bother to say what it gains him, because the point is the character itself. In a family full of lying tongues, this is the mirror opposite: an inner life that refuses to make speech a weapon.

narratives.narrative: Here deceit turns inward: the sense (D101) is 'he flatters himself about his sin', and the type (D102) is cognition - this is a movement of the knowing mind, a false internal reckoning, not merely spoken deceit. The bearer (D105) is the wicked (inferred), the man in whose heart transgression speaks and before whose eyes there is no fear of God (v1). The operation (D106) traces the process fully: he flatters himself in his own eyes that his iniquity cannot be found out and hated - self-deception about guilt. The target (D107) is self-flattery, and the coupling (D112) is 'flatter-himself', so the deceiver and the deceived are the same person - the interior lies to itself. The absences carry weight: source (D103, present:false) - no upstream cause is named because the flattery is self-generating, the mind is its own origin here; seat (D104) is 'none', so this is not organ-located but the whole self-regard gone crooked; manner (D108) 'none'; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) all present:false - the self-deceit is not graded and its downstream ruin, though it comes later in the psalm (v12), is not attached to this operation, keeping the lens on the interior act itself. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) names it precisely: the interior tells itself its sin is invisible and unhateable. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. This is deceit's most dangerous form in the family - falsehood aimed not at a neighbour or at God but at oneself, so that the man cannot even see his own guilt.
narratives.story: Here lying happens inside a person's own head. The wicked man talks himself into believing his sin will never be found out or hated - he soothes himself, flatters his own conscience, and looks the other way. The liar and the one being lied to are the same man: he is fooling himself. Nothing sets this off from outside; his own mind manufactures the comfortable falsehood, and it soaks the whole way he sees himself rather than sitting in one place. The passage does not stop to measure it or spell out where it leads, because the point is chilling enough on its own - this is deceit turned against the self, the kind that blinds a man to his own guilt.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is deceit / treachery (mirmah) - here concretised as 'the deceitful man' from whom David begs deliverance. The type (D102) is status: this is not an act being performed but a settled classification of a person, the interior guile that defines him. The bearer (D105) is the deceitful man (inferred). Crucially the operation (D106) is 'none' - explicitly no verb, no movement is recorded; the deceit is named as what he IS, not what he does at this moment. The target (D107) is likewise 'none', and manner (D108) 'none' - because a status, not an act, has no object and no style. The coupling (D112) is the one live relation: he is paired with the unjust man, so treachery and injustice stand together as the twin traits of the foe. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no interior origin is given for the treachery because it is presented as constitutive, the man's very make-up; seat (D104) 'none', not organ-located but whole-person; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) all present:false - the guile is unmeasured and its outworking is not traced, since the verse only labels the enemy, it does not narrate his scheme. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads mirmah as the inner treachery that defines the ungodly man from whom the psalmist seeks rescue. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. Read within the inner-being lens, the finding is that deceit can become identity: the man is not doing deceit, he is the deceitful one.
narratives.story: David is praying to be rescued from a treacherous man, and the striking thing is how the deceit is described - not as something the man is doing right now, but as simply who he is. He is 'the deceitful one', the way another might be called tall or old; the guile has hardened into his very identity. Because it is a label and not an action, there is no scheme to trace, no victim named, no method spelled out. The only thing tied to it is that he stands shoulder to shoulder with an unjust man - treachery and injustice as a matched pair. The lesson about the inner life is sobering: deceit can stop being something a person does and become something a person is.
narratives.variation_note: Of the three readings of H4820:deceitful (mirmah), this one alone renders it as a bare status with operation 'none' and no seat - deceit as the enemy's identity (43:1). It differs from #2 (Psa 52:4), where the same word is seated in 'the tongue' and names the organ of speech, and from #3 (Psa 109:2), typed as disposition and aimed at the psalmist in speech. The shift is from pure identity (here) to organ-located speech (52) to active hostile disposition (109).

narratives.narrative: This is the family's one clear positive-fidelity reading of falsehood, and it turns on a negation. The sense (D101) is to be false / deal falsely (shaqar), and the type (D102) is action - a covenant-act - but the action is denied: 'we have NOT been false to your covenant.' The bearer (D105) is the nation (inferred), the suffering community. The operation (D106) is 'be false (negated)', so the movement is asserted only to be cancelled - the interior did not do this. The target (D107) is 'your covenant' (a span pair), and the locus (D116) is unusually external:god - the fidelity is measured toward God, the arena being the covenant relationship. Coupling (D112) pairs it with not forgetting God (v17), welding faithfulness-in-speech to faithfulness-in-memory. The prohibition (D113) is the decisive present dimension here, and it is not 'none' as elsewhere but carries real content: 'negated (we have NOT been false to your covenant)' - the falsehood is explicitly ruled out of the interior. Absences: source (D103, present:false) and seat (D104) 'none' - the fidelity is whole-person, not organ-based; manner (D108) 'none'; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) all present:false - the faithfulness is not graded, and though it grounds the psalm's bewildered protest, no downstream effect is tagged to it. The discovery note (D114) frames it as covenant fidelity maintained under affliction, the ground of the nation's protest. Role (D115) characteristic. The finding: here falsehood is present only as the thing the inner being did NOT do - the bewildering point is that the interior stayed true and was crushed anyway.
narratives.story: This is the one bright note in a dark family. A whole suffering people insists that, for all their disaster, they have kept faith - they have not broken covenant with God, not forgotten him, not turned false. The falsehood appears here only as the very thing they did not do; it is flatly ruled out of their hearts. And that is exactly what makes their cry so raw: they stayed loyal in the one place loyalty is measured, toward God himself, and were still broken and shamed. Faithfulness of speech and faithfulness of memory stand together, unbowed - yet the reward looked like abandonment. The passage lets that uncomfortable truth stand without smoothing it over.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is deceit (mirmah), here the thing the tongue 'frames'. The type (D102) is status - the deceit named as a settled product - yet the operation (D106) supplies a verb by inference: 'frame / harness', the tongue harnessing lies like a smith. The bearer (D105) is the wicked, specifically his tongue (inferred), so the interior organ of speech is the actor. The target (D107) is 'none' - the deceit is framed but no single victim is attached to this dimension, though the next verses show the brother and mother's son slandered. The coupling (D112) pairs it with the mouth given free rein for evil (v19), so deceit and unbridled evil speech are a single flow. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no upstream interior cause is named, the deceit issues straight from a will already hating discipline (v17); seat (D104) 'none' as a flag even while the tongue does the framing - the deceit is not lodged in an organ as its home but produced by the speaking self; manner (D108) 'none'; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured, unnarrowed, its consequence held back for God's rebuke (v21) rather than tagged here. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads mirmah as the deceit the wicked's tongue weaves, slandering his brother. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding: deceit is manufactured - the tongue is a workshop, and the interior deliberately fashions falsehood against its own kin.
narratives.story: God is rebuking the wicked man, and one charge is that his tongue 'frames' deceit - it works lies the way a craftsman shapes metal. The picture is of an inner workshop: the mouth is given free rein for evil, and out of it the man deliberately manufactures falsehood, soon turning it against his own brother. No outside pressure is blamed; the lies come straight from a heart that already despises correction. The passage does not name a single victim at this point or measure how bad it is - it simply exposes the machinery. The unsettling insight is that deceit here is made on purpose, the tongue a factory turning out lies against the people closest to him.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is deceit / treachery (remiyyah), the falseness the tyrant 'works'. The type (D102) is status, but the operation (D106) adds the inferred verb 'work / practise' - deceit as a trade plied. The bearer (D105) is the tyrant (inferred), the mighty man who boasts of evil (v1). The target (D107) is 'none' at this dimension, and manner (D108) 'none' - the verse names the practice, not its object. The coupling (D112) is significant: this remiyyah is the deceitfulness voiced by the deceitful tongue of v4 (mirmah), so the two Hebrew terms in the one psalm are read as twin - the deceit worked and the deceitful tongue are one man's single vice. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no interior origin named, the treachery is his settled occupation; seat (D104) 'none' - not organ-fixed here (the tongue is named at v4/#9, not here); intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured, and the ruin (v5, God will break him) is God's response, not tagged to this operation. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads remiyyah (slackness/treachery) as the deceit he practises, a life built on lies. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding: deceit as a vocation - the interior does not merely lie once but has made falseness its craft, so that treachery is what the man is for.
narratives.story: The psalm confronts a powerful man who boasts about the evil he does, and it says his whole business is treachery - he 'works' deceit the way a labourer works a trade. His life is built on lies. In the same poem his tongue is called deceitful too, and the two descriptions point at one thing: this is a man whose falseness is not an occasional slip but his very occupation. The passage does not spell out his particular target here or weigh how deep it goes; it simply says this is what he does for a living. The insight into the inner life is that deceit can become a person's craft - practised, honed, and habitual until it defines him.
narratives.variation_note: Both readings of H7423:deceit (remiyyah) are typed by their setting. Here at Psa 52:2 it is a status/practice - deceit as the tyrant's trade, coupled to the deceitful tongue of the same psalm. At #2 (Psa 101:7) the same word is typed as a disposition and set in the king's house as something barred from God's presence. The difference is arena: here deceit is described in the doer (the tyrant plying it); there it is described being excluded by the righteous king.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is lying / falsehood (sheqer), preferred over righteous speech. The type (D102) is status, and the operation (D106) is the inferred verb 'loved / preferred' - so this is deceit read as an object of love, an inverted affection. The bearer (D105) is the tyrant (inferred). The manner (D108) is not 'none' here but carries content: 'more than speaking righteousness' - a comparative preference, love of the lie over the truth. The coupling (D112) pairs lying with loving evil over good (v3a), so the two clauses are one movement of a heart with reversed loves. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - the love of falsehood has no cause named upstream because it IS the interior orientation, the root not the fruit; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person, not organ; target (D107) 'none' - lying is loved as such, not directed at a victim in this line; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - the preference is stated, not graded, and its ruin waits for v5. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads sheqer as the lie the tyrant prefers to righteous speech - the verbal face of his inverted loves, deceit chosen for its own sake. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding is the deepest cut of the psalm: falsehood here is not a tool but a beloved - the interior does not merely use lies, it loves them more than the truth.
narratives.story: The most disturbing line about this tyrant is not that he lies but that he loves lying - he prefers falsehood to honest speech the way someone prefers one food to another. Alongside it, he loves evil more than good; the two go together as the tastes of a heart whose loves have been turned upside down. The passage does not aim the lie at a particular victim or measure its size, because the point is the affection itself. This is deceit not as a weapon picked up when useful, but as something wanted and enjoyed for its own sake. The insight is stark: the inner life can reach a point where it actually cherishes the lie over the truth.
narratives.variation_note: Among the three readings of H8267:lying (sheqer), this one alone reads it as a beloved object - operation 'loved/preferred', with an explicit comparative manner ('more than speaking righteousness'). It differs from #2 (Psa 109:2), where lying is an active hostile disposition spoken against the psalmist, and #3 (Psa 120:2), where it is the disposition of lying lips the psalmist begs deliverance from. Here the lie is loved; there it is done to a victim - preference versus assault.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is deceit / treachery (mirmah), here naming the 'deceitful tongue' itself. The type (D102) is status - the tongue's character - and uniquely in this cluster the seat (D104) is present and named: 'the tongue' (inferred). This is the one reading where deceit is explicitly organ-located, the interior vice fixed to the speaking member. The bearer (D105) is the tyrant (inferred). The operation (D106) is 'none' - no verb, because the verse addresses the tongue by its character rather than narrating an act. Target (D107) 'none', manner (D108) 'none' - a vocative naming, not a directed deed. The coupling (D112) ties this mirmah to the deceit worked in v2 (remiyyah), so the two words close a ring: what he practises (v2) is now his very name (v4). Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no upstream cause, the deceit is constitutive; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured, the destruction (v5) belonging to God's reply. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads mirmah as naming the tongue itself - the whole man summed in his lying speech. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding: deceit has so saturated the interior that the organ of speech is renamed after it - the man is addressed not as one who lies but as a 'deceitful tongue', vice become identity through the seat of speech.
narratives.story: By now the psalm no longer describes what the tyrant does; it simply calls him by his worst part - 'you deceitful tongue.' The lying has soaked so deep that his mouth itself becomes his name. This is the one place where the deceit is pinned to a specific part of him, the tongue, rather than left as a vague trait. What he was said to 'work' earlier in the psalm has now become who he is, the circle closing on itself. The verse names him rather than telling another story about him, and it does not measure or explain further. The insight is that a habit of lying can go so far that a person is finally identified with the very organ that speaks the lies.
narratives.variation_note: This is the only reading of H4820:deceitful (mirmah) where a seat is present - 'the tongue' - so deceit is organ-located and the man is named after his speaking member. It differs from #1 (Psa 43:1), a bare status with seat 'none' and no operation (deceit as pure identity of the enemy), and from #3 (Psa 109:2), a disposition aimed at the psalmist in speech. The progression is identity (43) to organ-fixed name (here) to active hostility (109).

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is fraud / deceit (mirmah), the falseness that fills the city's marketplace. The type (D102) is status - a pervasive condition, not a single act. The bearer (D105) is the city's wicked (inferred), a collective. The operation (D106) is 'none' - the verse describes fraud as an atmosphere that 'does not depart' rather than narrating a deed; target (D107) 'none' and manner (D108) 'none' accordingly. The coupling (D112) is the key relation: this civic mirmah is the same word as the betrayer's own treachery in v23, so the corruption of the public square and the treachery of the intimate friend (v13-14, v20-21) are read as one cloth. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no interior origin named for a condition that simply saturates the place; seat (D104) 'none' - not organ-located but ambient; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - the fraud is unmeasured and its outcome (the pit, v23) belongs to God's judgment, not tagged here. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads mirmah as the lying that props up the city's oppression, of one cloth with the betrayer's treachery. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding: deceit here is not one heart's act but a shared moral climate - fraud that never leaves the streets - and the psalm's shock is that the same interior falseness animates both the faceless city and the beloved friend who betrayed him.
narratives.story: The psalmist looks at his city and sees fraud that never leaves the marketplace - lying and cheating so constant they feel like the very air. It is not one person's single act but a whole climate of dishonesty hanging over the streets. The chilling twist is that the exact same falseness is what wounded him most personally: the friend who betrayed him (later in the psalm) is made of the same stuff as the corrupt city. So the deceit is both everywhere and intimate - in the crowd and in the companion. The passage does not weigh or explain it; it simply shows that the same rot fills a marketplace and a friendship alike.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is treachery / deceit (mirmah), the defining mark of the 'men of blood and treachery' who will not live out half their days. The type (D102) is status - treachery as a settled trait that classifies them. The bearer (D105) is the men of blood (inferred). The operation (D106) is 'none' - the verse labels them rather than narrating an act; target (D107) 'none', manner (D108) 'none'. The coupling (D112) explicitly binds this mirmah to the city's fraud (v11) and the betrayer's ways, so all three appearances in the psalm are read as one interior falseness. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no upstream cause, treachery is constitutive of who they are; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured. But there is a live implicit consequence in the text the note draws out: their treachery cuts short their own days. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads mirmah as the defining trait of the bloody men whose treachery shortens their lives. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding: treachery is here self-consuming - not merely a harm done to others but an interior falseness so corrosive that, by the psalm's reckoning, it curtails the deceiver's own lifespan. Deceit turns back on the deceiver.
narratives.story: At the close of the psalm the enemies are summed up as 'men of blood and treachery' - deceit is simply what they are. And here the passage adds a turn: their treachery does not only hurt others, it shortens their own lives, so that they will not live out half their days. The same falseness that filled the city and betrayed a friend earlier in the psalm is now their death sentence. It is not described as an act but as a brand on their character. The passage does not measure it or trace its steps; it just observes that this kind of dishonesty eats the dishonest. The insight is that treachery is self-consuming - it turns back on the one who lives by it.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is lies / falsehood (kazab), the speech of the wicked estranged from the womb. The type (D102) is status, and the operation (D106) is the inferred verb 'speak' - lying as utterance. The bearer (D105) is the wicked (inferred). Target (D107) 'none' and manner (D108) 'none' - the verse names their native speech, not a directed act. The coupling (D112) is the striking relation: lying is the immediate fruit of going astray from birth (v3), so falsehood is welded to an inborn estrangement - the lie is the first thing that comes out of a heart wrong from the start. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - and yet the text's own note supplies the deepest source-claim of the family: they go astray 'from the womb', 'from birth', so the falsehood has no proximate cause because its origin is native, congenital; seat (D104) 'none' - not organ-fixed but issuing from the whole estranged self; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads kazab as the native tongue of the wicked, untruth issuing from a heart astray from the start. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding is the family's most radical claim about origin: lying is not learned or provoked but inborn - the estranged interior speaks falsehood as its mother tongue.
narratives.story: This psalm makes the darkest claim about lying anywhere in the family: the wicked go wrong from the very womb, and lies are the first thing off their tongues. Falsehood here is not a habit picked up later or a reaction to being wronged - it is the native language of a heart that was crooked from birth. The passage does not aim the lies at anyone in particular or measure how bad they are; it is describing an origin, not an incident. Speaking untruth is simply what comes naturally out of an estranged inner life. The unsettling insight is that deceit can be spoken of as inborn - a mother tongue rather than a learned vice.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is to deal treacherously (bagad), of those who 'treacherously plot evil'. The type (D102) is action - here treachery is an active deed, not a static label. The bearer (D105) is the treacherous enemies (inferred), who lie in wait for the psalmist's life (v3). The operation (D106) is 'act treacherously / plot', and the target (D107) is 'evil' (a span pair) - so the movement runs from the treacherous interior toward the evil it designs. The coupling (D112) pairs the treachery with the evil they plot, welding faithless betrayal to malicious scheming. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no upstream cause named, though the psalm stresses the malice is 'for no transgression or sin of mine' (v3), i.e. causeless from the victim's side; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person, not organ; manner (D108) 'none'; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured, its outcome left to God's asked-for punishment (v5). Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads bagad (to betray / act faithlessly) as covenant-breaking wickedness God is asked not to spare - treachery joined to evil design. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding: treachery here is coupled to intention - it is not blind malice but faithlessness harnessed to a plan, an interior that betrays and schemes at once.
narratives.story: David prays against enemies who both betray and scheme - they 'treacherously plot evil.' The treachery here is active, a thing they are doing, and it is bound tight to the wickedness they are planning: faithlessness and calculation working together. What makes it worse is that the psalmist has given them no cause; the plotting springs from their own malice, not from any wrong of his. The passage does not measure the treachery or say exactly how it will end, leaving that to God's judgment. The insight into the inner life is that betrayal is not always hot-blooded - here it is cold and deliberate, a faithless heart yoked to a plan.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is lies / deceit (kachash), the falsehood the enemies utter. The type (D102) is status, and the operation (D106) is the inferred verb 'utter' - lying as spoken output. The bearer (D105) is the enemies (inferred), those 'bellowing with their mouths, with swords in their lips' (v7). Notably the seat (D104) is present here: 'the mouth' (inferred) - so this lie is organ-located, lodged in the speaking mouth, one of the few readings that fix falsehood to an organ. The target (D107) is 'none', manner (D108) 'none'. The coupling (D112) pairs the lies with the cursing they utter, so deceit and cursing are twin sins of the mouth. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no upstream cause, the lie flows from their pride (v12, 'let them be trapped in their pride'); intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured, the consuming wrath (v13) being God's response rather than a tagged effect. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads kachash as the deceit twinned with cursing - the mouth's sin that, with their pride, brings God's consuming wrath. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding: this lie is a sin of the mouth specifically, paired with cursing and rooted in pride - deceit as one strand of an arrogant, corrupt speech.
narratives.story: The enemies here are all mouth - bellowing, with swords in their lips - and out of that mouth come lies twinned with curses. This time the deceit is pinned to the organ that speaks it: the lie lives in the mouth. It rises out of their pride, and cursing rides along with it, the two forming a single ugly stream of speech. The passage does not aim the lie at a named victim or measure it; it simply exposes the arrogant, foul-mouthed source, then hands the outcome over to God's judgment. The insight is that deceit often travels in company - here it comes bundled with cursing and pride as the sins of a boastful mouth.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is falsehood / lie (kazab), in which the enemies 'take pleasure'. The type (D102) is status, and the operation (D106) is the inferred verb 'delighted in' - so, like Psa 52:3, falsehood appears as an object of pleasure, an inverted delight. The bearer (D105) is the enemies (inferred). Target (D107) 'none' and manner (D108) 'none'. The coupling (D112) is doubly revealing: falsehood is the object of their pleasure and it is expressed in the false blessing - 'they bless with their mouths, but inwardly they curse' (v4). So the interior falseness is defined precisely as a split between outer word and inner heart. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no upstream cause, the delight in the lie IS the orientation; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads kazab as the falsehood they love, showing in blessing with the mouth while cursing within. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding: this is deceit as a divided self - the mouth blesses while the heart curses - and the psalm's diagnosis is that they LOVE this doubleness. Falsehood is not just told; it is enjoyed, and it takes the specific shape of a hypocrite's split interior.
narratives.story: These enemies actually enjoy falsehood - they take pleasure in the lie. And the passage shows exactly what that looks like: they bless with their mouths while cursing inside. The deceit here is a divided self, one face for the world and another underneath, and the horror is that they delight in living that way. The falseness is not aimed or measured; it is simply loved for its own sake. The insight into the inner life is sharp: hypocrisy is a lie a person tells with the outside while the inside says the opposite - and it can become something the heart actually relishes.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is lies / falsehood (sheqer), the weapon of those who attack the psalmist. The type (D102) is status, and the operation (D106) is the inferred verb 'attack with' - here falsehood is instrumental, a weapon wielded. The bearer (D105) is the enemies (inferred), 'more in number than the hairs of my head.' Uniquely for the sheqer readings, the target (D107) is present and personal: 'the psalmist' (inferred) - the lie is aimed straight at him. The coupling (D112) pairs the lies with the causeless hatred (v4, 'those who hate me without cause'), so false accusation and groundless hatred are one movement. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no cause named, and indeed the whole point is causelessness; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person; manner (D108) 'none'; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured, though the note observes the lie is pressed as if it were justice ('what I did not steal must I now restore?', v4). Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads sheqer as the lies with which the mighty foes assail him, falsehood pressed as if it were justice. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding: falsehood as assault - a lie deployed as a weapon of false accusation against an innocent man, and disguised as a rightful claim.
narratives.story: The psalmist is surrounded by enemies who attack him with lies - false accusations hurled at him as if they were weapons. He is made to answer for things he never did, forced to 'restore' what he never stole. The lies are bound up with a hatred that has no cause; they hate him for nothing and then invent charges to justify it. The passage does not measure the falsehood or explain where it comes from; the cruelty is precisely that it is baseless, yet dressed up to look like justice. The insight is that deceit can be a weapon of assault - a lie aimed at an innocent person and disguised as a rightful demand.
narratives.variation_note: The three readings of H8267:lie (sheqer) differ by how the lie functions. Here at Psa 69:4 it is a weapon of assault aimed personally at the psalmist ('attack me with lies'), typed as status. At #2 (Psa 101:7) it is an act the righteous king bars from his house. At #3 (Psa 119:69) it is the slander the insolent smear him with while he keeps God's precepts. Here the lie strikes an innocent as false accusation; in 101 it is excluded by authority; in 119 it is endured under devotion.

narratives.narrative: This is treachery read in the negative - a betrayal refused. The sense (D101) is to betray / deal faithlessly (bagad), 'I would have betrayed the generation of your children.' The type (D102) is action, but the operation (D106) is 'betray (hypothetically, avoided)' - the deed is entertained only to be renounced. The bearer (D105) is the psalmist himself, which he refrained from (inferred). The target (D107) is 'the generation of God's children' (inferred), the community of faith. The manner (D108) is present and specific: 'by voicing his doubt aloud' - the betrayal would have been an act of speech, publishing his crisis. The coupling (D112) is the restraint that held him back from speaking his doubt. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - the impulse's origin is his own wearisome inner struggle (v16), but no discrete cause is tagged; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - the avoided act has no measured force and no downstream effect precisely because it was not done. Prohibition (D113) absent as a flag, though the whole reading is a self-imposed restraint. The discovery note (D114) reads bagad as the faithlessness to God's people he refused to commit - loving the community enough to hold his tongue while he wrestled. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding: treachery here is a road not taken - the interior, in crisis, chooses not to scatter others' faith with its own doubt. Faithfulness is defined as costly silence.
narratives.story: The psalmist is in a spiritual crisis, tempted to broadcast his doubts about whether faith is worth it. But he checks himself: if he had spoken that way, he would have betrayed God's people, unsettling their faith with his own. So the betrayal here is one he almost commits and then refuses - a treachery of the tongue held back. He loves the community enough to stay silent and wrestle privately rather than spread his despair. Because he never does it, there is nothing to measure and no damage done. The insight into the inner life is quiet but powerful: sometimes faithfulness is a betrayal you choose not to speak, holding your tongue for others' sake while you struggle.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is to lie (kazab), of a people who 'lied to him with their tongues.' The type (D102) is action - an act performed. The bearer (D105) is 'they' (inferred), the wilderness generation who, when God killed them, sought him and repented (v34-35). The operation (D106) is 'lie', and the target (D107) is 'to God with their tongues' (inferred) - so the falsehood is aimed Godward, and fittingly the locus (D116) is external:god. The manner (D108) is 'none'. The coupling (D112) pairs the lying with the flattering mouth of the same verse, so lying and flattery are twin faces of a false repentance. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no upstream cause tagged, but the note exposes the root: the repentance was not seated in the heart; seat (D104) 'none' as a flag - and this is the very point, the lie was on the tongue and NOT in the heart, so the absence of an interior seat is itself the finding; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads kazab as the falsehood of a repentance not seated in the heart. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) external:god. The inner-being finding: this is deceit aimed at God in worship - a repentance that is all tongue and no heart. The unseated lie is the exact hollowness the psalm exposes: words of return with no interior behind them.
narratives.story: After God disciplines them, the people turn back to him - but only with their mouths. They flatter him and lie to him with their tongues while their hearts are unchanged. This is deceit aimed straight at God in the act of worship, a repentance that is all words and no interior. The telling thing is that the lie sits on the tongue and never reaches the heart; the emptiness is the whole point. The passage does not measure it or explain its cause beyond that hollowness. The insight into the inner life is uncomfortable: a person can 'repent' loudly to God and still be lying, because true return has to live in the heart, not just the mouth.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is to flatter / deceive (pathah), of a people who 'flattered him with their mouths.' The type (D102) is action. The bearer (D105) is 'they' (inferred), the same wilderness generation. The operation (D106) is 'flatter / coax', and the target (D107) is 'God with their mouths' (inferred); the locus (D116) is external:god - the coaxing aimed Godward. Manner (D108) 'none'. The coupling (D112) pairs the flattery with the lying tongue and unsteady heart, so this reading is the twin of H3576:lied#1 in the same verse - and the two must be preserved as distinct (directive 8): flattery (pathah, a coaxing seduction) is not identical to lying (kazab, plain falsehood). Flattery is the smoother, more manipulative movement - words that court and cajole rather than merely misstate. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no cause tagged; seat (D104) 'none' - the coaxing is on the mouth, not the heart, again making the absent interior seat the point; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads pathah as the hollow, coaxing words masking an unchanged heart. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) external:god. The inner-being finding: flattery is deceit's ingratiating mode - the interior tries to win God with soft, courting speech while remaining unchanged. Distinct from the flat lie beside it, this is manipulation dressed as devotion.
narratives.story: In the same breath as their lying, the people 'flatter' God - they coax him with smooth, courting words, trying to win him over while their hearts stay exactly as they were. Flattery is a slightly different thing from a plain lie: it is the seducing, ingratiating kind of falseness, words designed to charm rather than simply to deceive. Here it is aimed at God himself, a soft-spoken devotion with nothing behind it. Like the lie beside it, the flattery lives on the mouth and never touches the heart, and the passage leaves it unmeasured. The insight is that deceit has a smooth, manipulative face too - a person can try to flatter even God with hollow, coaxing words.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is to act treacherously (bagad), of a people who 'turned away and acted treacherously like their fathers.' The type (D102) is action - a committed deed, the opposite pole to the avoided betrayal of Psa 73:15. The bearer (D105) is 'they' (inferred), Israel after the conquest. The operation (D106) is 'betray / deal faithlessly', and the target (D107) is 'with God' (inferred); the locus (D116) is external:god - treachery aimed at the covenant Lord. Manner (D108) 'none'. The coupling (D112) pairs the treachery with 'turning away' (v57), so apostasy and faithlessness are one motion. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - and yet the note names an inherited origin: 'like their fathers', a family likeness of sin, so the falseness is generational; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured, God's wrath and rejection (v59) being the response rather than a tagged effect. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads bagad as faithless betrayal, the family likeness of sin. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) external:god. The inner-being finding: here treachery is committed, covenantal, and hereditary - the interior betrays God as its fathers did, so faithlessness is passed down like a trait. Contrast with the refused betrayal of Psa 73:15 sharpens the point: the same word names both the treachery embraced and the treachery declined.
narratives.story: Looking back over Israel's history, the psalm says the people 'turned away and acted treacherously, just like their fathers.' This is betrayal actually done - and done against God himself, breaking faith with the one who rescued them. What stands out is that it runs in the family: they betray the way their fathers betrayed, as if faithlessness were inherited. The passage does not measure it; God's anger is the response, not part of the description. Set beside the psalmist elsewhere who refused to betray, it shows the same word cutting two ways. The insight is that treachery can be a family inheritance - a pattern of breaking faith with God handed down from one generation to the next.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is to be deceitful (remiyah), imaged as 'they twisted like a deceitful bow.' The type (D102) is status - a settled unreliability. The bearer (D105) is 'they' (inferred), the same treacherous generation. The operation (D106) is 'prove false', and the target (D107) is the vivid simile 'like a slack bow' (inferred) - a bow that warps and fails its aim. The manner (D108) is 'none'. The coupling (D112) pairs this deceitfulness with the treachery of the same verse (H0898 above), so 'acted treacherously' and 'twisted like a deceitful bow' are one interior fact stated twice - preserved as distinct (directive 8): the first names the act of betrayal, this one names the character of unreliability behind it. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no upstream cause; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads remiyah as treachery imaged as a warped bow that fails its aim. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding: deceitfulness here is unreliability - a bow that cannot be trusted to shoot true. The image locates the vice not in an aggressive lie but in a failure of dependability: the interior bends and betrays under tension, useless to the one who would rely on it.
narratives.story: The same verse compares the faithless people to 'a deceitful bow' - a bow so warped it can never shoot straight. Alongside their outright betrayal, this picture captures something quieter: they simply cannot be relied on. Draw them tight and they twist; aim them and they fail. The deceit here is less an attack than a deep unreliability, a character that bends and gives way exactly when it should hold. The passage does not measure it or trace its cause; the warped bow says it all. The insight into the inner life is that deceit is not only the lie a person tells but the untrustworthiness of a person who can never be counted on to hold true.
narratives.variation_note: Among the three readings of H7423:deceitful (remiyah), this one uniquely images the vice as unreliability - 'a deceitful bow' that warps and fails its aim, coupled to the generation's treachery against God (locus external in the same verse's arc). It differs from #2 (Psa 120:2) and #3 (Psa 120:3), where the same word names a hostile 'deceitful tongue' aimed at the psalmist. Here deceit is a failure of dependability; in Psalm 120 it is active verbal aggression.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is to cringe (kachash), of those who hate the Lord who 'would cringe toward him.' The type (D102) is action, and the operation (D106) is 'cringe / feign submission' - a movement of forced, false homage. The bearer (D105) is the haters (inferred), 'those who hate the Lord.' The target (D107) is 'before God' (inferred), and the locus (D116) is external:god - the cringing aimed Godward. Manner (D108) 'none'. The coupling (D112) pairs the cringing with the hatred, and that pairing is the whole finding: the ones who cringe are the ones who hate, so the submission is a lie. This is deceit in the mode of feigned homage - outward bowing without inward love, the body performing a loyalty the heart denies. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - the cringing is compelled by defeat, not sprung from an inner cause; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads kachash as the forced, feigned submission of the cowed foe, homage without love. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) external:god. The inner-being finding: falsehood here is a lie of the body toward God - the defeated enemy performs submission while still hating. Deceit and hatred coexist in one act, the outward cringe masking the unchanged interior.
narratives.story: God says that if his people would only listen, their enemies - the very ones who hate him - would come cringing to him. But that cringing is not real love; it is the forced bow of a beaten foe, homage put on for show while the hatred stays underneath. It is a lie told with the body: the knees bend toward God while the heart still despises him. The passage does not measure it or explain what drives it beyond defeat. The insight into the inner life is that submission itself can be a form of deceit - a person can outwardly cringe before God while inwardly hating him, the gesture and the heart pulling opposite ways.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is vanity (shav), 'for what vanity you have created all mankind!' The type (D102) is state - a condition of being, not an act of deceit. This reading stretches the family: shav here is not a lie told but the emptiness/frailty of human existence. The bearer (D105) is all mankind (inferred). The operation (D106) is 'be created in vanity', and the target (D107) is 'transient' (inferred) - the movement is toward fleetingness, mortality. Manner (D108) 'none'. The coupling (D112) pairs the vanity with the reflection on mortality (v47-48, 'what man can live and never see death?'). Absences: source (D103, present:false) - the cause of the vanity is, uncomfortably, God's own creating ('you have created'), but no interior source is tagged because the emptiness is a given of the human condition, not a self-generated fault; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads shav as the frailty and fleetingness of human life, the ground of the plea to remember. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding: 'vanity' here names not falsehood but futility - the interior's honest reckoning that human life is a breath, short and fragile. Within the family this widens deceit-falsehood toward emptiness: what is 'vain' is not a lie but a life that vanishes.
narratives.story: In the depths of a lament, the psalmist cries out over how fleeting human life is: 'for what emptiness you have made everyone!' Here 'vanity' is not a lie someone tells but the sheer frailty of being human - a life that is here and gone, unable to escape death. It is an honest reckoning with mortality, the ground of the plea for God to remember how short a person's days are. The passage does not soften the discomfort that it is God himself who made us this fleeting. The insight into the inner life is that emptiness can be faced squarely: the heart can look at how brief and fragile life is and say so plainly, without pretending otherwise.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is to slander (lashan), 'whoever slanders his neighbour secretly.' The type (D102) is action. The bearer (D105) is the slanderer (inferred). The operation (D106) is 'slander secretly', and the target (D107) is 'his neighbour' (inferred) - so the movement runs from a hidden interior toward the neighbour's reputation. The key qualifier is the secrecy embedded in the operation: the slander is done in the dark, which marks it as covert deceit. Manner (D108) 'none' as a separate flag (the 'secretly' is carried in the operation itself). The coupling (D112) and locus (D116) both carry the value 'internal:ib-state' with the note that the slanderer is paired with being destroyed by the king - so the interior vice is set against the king's judgment: 'whoever slanders his neighbour secretly I will destroy.' Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no upstream cause named; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured. Prohibition (D113) absent as a flag, though the king's intolerance functions as a ban. The discovery note (D114) reads lashan as the secret defamer, the vice the king will not tolerate. Role (D115) characteristic. The inner-being finding: slander here is deceit's covert species - defamation whispered in secret, and it is precisely the hiddenness that makes it a matter of the interior. The righteous king's stance is that this hidden vice cannot dwell near him.
narratives.story: The king of this psalm is setting the rules for his own household and his own heart, and he names one vice he will not tolerate: the person who slanders a neighbour in secret. What marks this out is the secrecy - the damage is done in the dark, behind the victim's back, which makes it a hidden thing of the heart. The king's answer is blunt: whoever does it, he will destroy. The passage does not trace the slanderer's motive or measure his words; it simply exposes the covert defamer. The insight into the inner life is that some deceit does its worst quietly and unseen - and a person of integrity refuses to let that whispering vice live anywhere near them.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is deceit (remiyah), 'no one who practises deceit shall dwell in my house.' The type (D102) is disposition - a settled bent, here viewed as the thing barred. The bearer (D105) is the deceitful (inferred). The operation (D106) is 'practise deceit', and the target (D107) is 'in the king's house' (inferred) - the arena from which it is excluded. Manner (D108) 'none'. The coupling (D112) and locus (D116) carry 'internal:ib-state' with the note that this deceit is paired with the liar expelled (v7b) - so the deceiver and the liar are barred together. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no upstream cause; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured. Prohibition (D113) absent as a flag, but the whole verse is functionally a prohibition: the king's house has no room for the deceitful. The discovery note (D114) reads remiyah as the treachery the king bars from his presence. Role (D115) characteristic. The inner-being finding: deceit is here viewed from the side of the one who refuses it - not narrated in a deceiver's act but named as a disposition excluded from the community of the righteous king. The reading defines integrity negatively: to be near the king is to be a place where deceit cannot dwell.
narratives.story: The righteous king lays down who may live in his house, and he shuts the door on deceit: no one who practises it will dwell with him. Here deceit is seen from the other side - not a scheme being carried out, but a settled bent that the king simply will not have around him. The deceiver and the liar are turned away together. The passage does not tell a story about a particular deceiver or measure his guile; it defines the king's household by what it excludes. The insight into the inner life is that integrity can be described by what it refuses to keep company with: to stay close to what is good is to become a place where deceit finds no room.
narratives.variation_note: This second reading of H7423:deceit (remiyah) is typed as a disposition being excluded - deceit barred from the king's house and paired with the expelled liar (Psa 101:7). It differs from #1 (Psa 52:2), where the same word is the tyrant's practised trade, the deceit he actively works. The shift is of vantage point: at 52 deceit is described in the doer who plies it; here it is described by the righteous authority who refuses it entry.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is lies (sheqer), 'no one who utters lies shall continue before my eyes.' The type (D102) is action. The bearer (D105) is the liar (inferred). The operation (D106) is 'utter lies', and the target (D107) is 'before the king' (inferred) - the arena of exclusion. Manner (D108) 'none'. The coupling (D112) and locus (D116) carry 'internal:ib-state' with the note that this lying is paired with the deceit expelled (v7a) - so, preserved as distinct from H7423:deceit#2 in the same verse (directive 8): 'practising deceit' names the disposition, 'uttering lies' names the specific verbal act. The two are barred together but not identical - one is the bent, one is the spoken output. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no upstream cause; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured. Prohibition (D113) absent as a flag, the verse functioning as the king's ban. The discovery note (D114) reads sheqer as the falsehood the king will not let stand. Role (D115) characteristic. The inner-being finding: the lie here is judged by an authority that will not let it 'continue before my eyes' - falsehood exposed to a steady gaze cannot endure. Deceit is defined not by its telling but by its inability to survive in the presence of integrity.
narratives.story: In the same breath the king bars the liar: no one who tells lies will last in his sight. Where the previous line shut out the settled bent toward deceit, this line targets the actual spoken lie - the falsehood as it leaves the mouth. The two are turned away side by side, but they are not quite the same: one is the crooked bent of the heart, the other is the lie itself. The passage does not measure the lies or explain them; it simply says they cannot go on under the king's steady gaze. The insight into the inner life is that falsehood cannot bear to be watched by integrity - held under an honest eye, a lie has no room to continue.
narratives.variation_note: This second reading of H8267:lie (sheqer) is an act excluded by the righteous king - the uttered lie that cannot continue before his eyes (Psa 101:7). It differs from #1 (Psa 69:4), where the lie is a weapon of assault aimed at the innocent psalmist, and from #3 (Psa 119:69), where it is the slander the devout man endures. Here authority refuses the lie; there the lie strikes or wounds a victim - exclusion versus attack.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is vain (shav), 'for vain is the salvation of man!' The type (D102) is disposition - here a considered judgement of the interior, not a lie. The bearer (D105) is the psalmist (inferred). The operation (D106) is 'reckon human help vain', and the target (D107) is 'against God's' (inferred) - so the movement is a weighing: human deliverance set against divine and found empty. Manner (D108) 'none'. The coupling (D112) and locus (D116) carry 'internal:ib-state' with the note that the vanity is paired with doing valiantly through God (v13) - the empty human help contrasted with the effective help of God. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no cause tagged, the reckoning is a settled conviction; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads shav as the reckoning that human help is worthless, confidence turned from man to God. Role (D115) characteristic. The inner-being finding: 'vain' here is a movement of trust, not deceit - the interior judges the emptiness of relying on man and redirects its confidence to God. This is the family's word for falsehood/emptiness turned to a truthful use: naming a real void so as to lean where help is solid.
narratives.story: Facing enemies and feeling abandoned, the psalmist reaches a clear-eyed verdict: human help is empty - 'vain is the salvation of man.' This is not a lie but an honest judgement, a decision about where to put his trust. He weighs what people can do against what God can do and finds human rescue worthless by comparison, then turns to God, with whom he will 'do valiantly.' The passage does not measure the feeling or trace its cause; it is a settled conviction. The insight into the inner life is that naming an emptiness can be an act of faith: seeing plainly that some things cannot save you frees the heart to lean on the One who can.
narratives.variation_note: Of the four H7723:vain (shav) readings, this one alone is a disposition of trust - the psalmist's reckoning that human salvation is empty, redirecting confidence to God (Psa 108:12). It differs from #2, #3, #4 (Psa 127:1-2), where the same word describes the futility of human labour, watching, and toil done without God. Here 'vain' is a judgement the heart makes about where to trust; in Psalm 127 it is the emptiness of effort itself apart from God's action.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is deceitful (mirmah), 'wicked and deceitful mouths are opened against me.' The type (D102) is disposition - an active hostile bent. The bearer (D105) is the enemies (inferred). The operation (D106) is 'be deceitful', and the target (D107) is 'in speech' (inferred), with the coupling (D112) and locus (D116) noting it is paired with the wicked and lying mouths (v2). So the movement runs from a deceitful interior out through hostile speech aimed at the psalmist, who returns love and prayer for their accusation (v4-5). Manner (D108) 'none'. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no upstream cause, and the psalm stresses the hostility is 'without cause' (v3) and in return for love (v5), so it is causeless from the victim's side; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads mirmah as the treachery of the enemies' speech. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding: deceit here is weaponised hostility - a deceitful disposition that opens the mouth against an innocent who has shown only love. The sharp edge is the exchange: love met with deceitful accusation, good repaid with treachery.
narratives.story: The psalmist is under attack by 'wicked and deceitful mouths' - enemies whose treachery pours out as false accusation against him. What makes it bite is his own response: he has loved them, and he gives himself to prayer, yet they repay his love with lies and hatred. The deceit is an active hostility, a crooked heart turned into hostile speech, and it comes without any cause he has given. The passage does not measure it or explain its origin beyond that groundlessness. The insight into the inner life is that deceit can be pure ingratitude weaponised - a treacherous heart that answers kindness with slander, good with betrayal.
narratives.variation_note: This third reading of H4820:deceitful (mirmah) is typed as a hostile disposition aimed at the psalmist through speech, sharpened by the exchange of love for treachery (Psa 109:2). It differs from #1 (Psa 43:1), a bare status naming the enemy's identity with no operation, and #2 (Psa 52:4), where the word is seated in 'the tongue' and names the man after his speaking organ. The progression across the three is identity (43) to organ-fixed name (52) to active hostility repaying love with lies (109).

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is lying (sheqer), 'speaking against me with lying tongues.' The type (D102) is disposition - an active hostile bent. The bearer (D105) is the enemies (inferred). The operation (D106) is 'speak lies', and the target (D107) is 'against the psalmist' (inferred); the coupling (D112) and locus (D116) note it is paired with the deceit (the deceitful mouths of the same verse). This must be preserved as distinct from H4820:deceitful#3 in the same verse (directive 8): 'deceitful mouths' names the treacherous character of the organ, 'lying tongues' names the specific false speech coming from it - the disposition and its verbal act, twin but not identical. Manner (D108) 'none'. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - causeless from the victim's side (v3-5); seat (D104) 'none' as a flag despite 'tongues' being the instrument - the lie is not lodged in an organ as its home but produced by the hostile self; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads sheqer as the falsehood of the foes' accusations. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding: lying here is the spoken discharge of a deceitful disposition - false accusation aimed at an innocent, the verbal weapon paired with the treacherous mouth that fires it.
narratives.story: In the same verse the enemies speak against the psalmist 'with lying tongues.' Where their mouths were called treacherous, here the focus narrows to what those mouths actually say - the false accusations themselves. The two go together but are not the same: one is the crooked character, the other is the lie it produces. And, as with the deceit beside it, the psalmist has done nothing to earn it. The passage does not measure the lies or trace their source. The insight into the inner life is that a treacherous heart and a lying tongue work as a pair - the deceit inside becomes the false word outside, both aimed at someone who never gave them cause.
narratives.variation_note: This second reading of H8267:lying (sheqer) is the spoken discharge of hostility - 'lying tongues' aimed at the psalmist, paired with the deceitful mouths of the same verse (Psa 109:2). It differs from #1 (Psa 52:3), where lying is a beloved object preferred to righteous speech, and #3 (Psa 120:2), where it is the lying lips the psalmist begs deliverance from. Here the lie is an active assault; at 52 it is cherished; at 120 it is the thing prayed against.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is liars (kazab), 'All mankind are liars.' The type (D102) is status - a sweeping classification of humanity. The bearer (D105) is all mankind (inferred). The operation (D106) is 'be liars', and the target (D107) is 'untrustworthy' (inferred) - the verdict that people cannot be relied on. Manner (D108) 'none'. The coupling (D112) and locus (D116) note the verdict is 'paired with the alarm' - it is spoken 'in my alarm' (v11), a judgement uttered from a place of distress. This is important: the reading is grounded in the psalmist's rushed, alarmed state, so the universal indictment is read as an interior cry under pressure, not a cool doctrine. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no cause named beyond the alarm; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads kazab as the verdict of the alarmed, human faithlessness weighed against God's truth. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding: here 'liars' is the interior's blanket verdict on humanity, spoken in alarm - a felt truth that all people are unreliable, set (in the psalm's arc) against the God who has proved trustworthy (v1-9). Deceit is universalised as the human condition seen from within a crisis.
narratives.story: Rescued from the brink of death, the psalmist recalls the sweeping thing he blurted out in his panic: 'Everyone is a liar.' It is a verdict spoken in alarm - a felt cry that no human being can really be trusted, thrown out from the middle of distress rather than worked out in calm. Set against the psalm's larger story, it throws God's reliability into relief: people fail you, but the Lord heard and delivered. The passage does not measure the judgement or defend it; it simply reports the honest, rattled thing a desperate heart said. The insight into the inner life is that crisis can push a person to a bleak universal verdict on others - and that such cries are real, even as they drive the heart to lean on the one who does not lie.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is falsehood / false way (sheqer), 'Put false ways far from me.' The type (D102) is disposition - the false way as a bent to be removed. The bearer (D105) is the foes / the false way (inferred) - notably ambiguous, the falsehood belonging both to hostile others and to a way the psalmist himself begs God to keep from him. The operation (D106) is 'lie / deceive', and the target (D107) is 'against the psalmist and the truth' (inferred). Manner (D108) 'none'. The coupling (D112) pairs it with the whole FALSEHOOD arc of Psalm 119 - the sheqer that recurs across the psalm (this reading is the anchor for the recurrences at v104 and v128). Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no upstream cause; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured. Prohibition (D113) absent as a flag, though the petition 'put false ways far from me' is functionally a prayer for prohibition. The discovery note (D114) reads sheqer as the false way the psalmist begs God to remove. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding: falsehood here is a way that can attach to the self, and the interior's response is petition - not merely hating the lie in enemies but asking God to hold it far from one's own path. Deceit is treated as a moral direction the heart must be guarded against, and the same conviction recurs twice more in the psalm (v104, v128), showing it as a sustained interior stance rather than a single moment.
narratives.story: In this stretch of the long psalm about God's law, the psalmist prays, 'Keep false ways far from me.' Falsehood here is pictured as a road a person could end up walking - and rather than only condemning it in his enemies, he asks God to keep it away from his own feet. It is a plea for protection from a moral direction, a way of life that lies. This same conviction comes back later in the psalm, at two more points, so it is not a passing thought but a settled stance he keeps returning to. The passage does not measure the falsehood or trace its origin. The insight into the inner life is that guarding against deceit starts with one's own path: the honest heart prays to be kept off the false road, not just to spot it in others.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is falsehood / false way (sheqer), 'the insolent smear me with lies.' The type (D102) is disposition. The bearer (D105) is the foes / the false way (inferred) - here the insolent, the proud. The operation (D106) is 'lie / deceive', and the target (D107) is 'against the psalmist and the truth' (inferred). Manner (D108) 'none'. The coupling (D112) pairs it with the whole FALSEHOOD arc of Psalm 119. The distinctive note is the counter-movement in the verse itself: 'the insolent smear me with lies, BUT with my whole heart I keep your precepts' - so the reading holds two interiors at once, the proud liar and the wholehearted keeper. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no upstream cause; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads sheqer as the slander of the proud. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding: falsehood here is the slander of arrogance - the insolent smear the devout with lies - and the finding is set precisely against the psalmist's wholehearted fidelity. Deceit assaults from without while integrity holds within; the lie does not penetrate the kept heart.
narratives.story: The proud and insolent smear the psalmist with lies, dragging his name through falsehood. But the verse sets that against something steadier: while they smear him, he keeps God's precepts with his whole heart. Two inner lives stand side by side - the arrogant liar outside and the wholehearted believer within - and the lies, for all their malice, do not shift him. The passage does not measure the slander or explain where the pride comes from. The insight into the inner life is that falsehood can be hurled at a person from the outside without ever conquering the inside: a heart set wholly on what is good can be smeared and still hold firm.
narratives.variation_note: This third reading of H8267:lie (sheqer) is the slander of the insolent endured under devotion - lies smeared on the psalmist while he keeps God's precepts wholeheartedly (Psa 119:69). It differs from #1 (Psa 69:4), where the lie is a weapon of false accusation striking an innocent, and #2 (Psa 101:7), where it is an act the righteous king bars from his house. Here the lie is borne without dislodging the kept heart; in 69 it wounds, in 101 it is excluded by authority.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is falsehood / false way (sheqer), 'they have wronged me with falsehood.' The type (D102) is disposition. The bearer (D105) is the foes / the false way (inferred), the insolent. The operation (D106) is 'lie / deceive', and the target (D107) is 'against the psalmist and the truth' (inferred). Manner (D108) 'none'. The coupling (D112) pairs it with the whole FALSEHOOD arc of Psalm 119; this reading is the anchor for the recurrences at v86 and v163. The verse's counter-movement is again present: 'let the insolent be put to shame, because they have wronged me with falsehood; as for me, I will meditate on your precepts' - so the response to being lied against is not counter-deceit but meditation. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no upstream cause; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads sheqer as the lie by which the foes wronged him. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding: falsehood here is an injury - the foes 'wronged me with falsehood' - and the interior's answer is to turn to meditation rather than retaliation. The lie is a wound, but the wounded heart does not reply with a lie; it withdraws into what is true. This conviction recurs across the psalm (v86, v163), a sustained interior posture toward being deceived.
narratives.story: The psalmist has been genuinely wronged - the arrogant have injured him with lies. Yet his reaction is striking: instead of fighting falsehood with falsehood, he says, 'as for me, I will meditate on your precepts.' He leaves their shaming to God and turns inward toward what is true. The lie is a real wound, but he refuses to answer it in kind, and this same posture shows up again elsewhere in the psalm, making it a steady habit of his heart. The passage does not measure the falsehood or explain its source. The insight into the inner life is that the right answer to being lied about may be to steady yourself on the truth rather than to strike back with a lie of your own.

narratives.narrative: The sense (D101) is falsehood / false way (sheqer), 'their cunning is in vain' - the deceit of those who stray from God's statutes. The type (D102) is disposition. The bearer (D105) is the foes / the false way (inferred), the strayers whom God spurns. The operation (D106) is 'lie / deceive', and the target (D107) is 'against the psalmist and the truth' (inferred). Manner (D108) 'none'. The coupling (D112) pairs it with the whole FALSEHOOD arc of Psalm 119. The distinctive turn is the futility verdict: the strayers' cunning (their sheqer) 'is in vain' - God spurns them and discards the wicked 'like dross' (v118-119). So the deceit is not only condemned but shown to be self-defeating. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no upstream cause; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured, though the note stresses the deceit's futility. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads sheqer as the vain deceit of the strayers. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding: falsehood here is exposed as futile - the cunning of those who abandon the truth comes to nothing before God, who sifts them out like waste. Deceit is not merely wrong but empty; the schemer's guile is spent on an outcome God overturns.
narratives.story: The psalmist watches those who wander away from God and work their cunning schemes, and he sees how it ends: their trickery is 'in vain.' God spurns them and throws out the wicked like the worthless scrap left after melting metal. So their deceit is not only wrong but useless - all that scheming buys them nothing but rejection. The passage does not measure the falsehood or explain its roots; it simply exposes how empty it proves. The insight into the inner life is that deceit is finally futile: however clever the lie, a life built on it is discarded like dross, and the schemer's guile comes to nothing.

narratives.narrative: This reading turns the family inside out: the char is not a lie but the loathing of it. The sense (D101) is to abhor (taab), 'I hate and abhor falsehood, but I love your law.' The type (D102) is disposition - a settled affection of aversion. The bearer (D105) is the psalmist (inferred). The operation (D106) is 'abhor falsehood', and the target (D107) is 'none' as a flag though the object is plainly falsehood itself - the verse names the loathing without objectifying a further target beyond the sheqer it recoils from. Manner (D108) 'none'. The coupling (D112) pairs the abhorrence within its char-arc across the psalm, and the verse itself couples it with love: hatred of falsehood set against love of God's law, the two poles of one oriented heart. Absences: source (D103, present:false) - no upstream cause, the aversion is a settled orientation; seat (D104) 'none' - whole-person; intensity (D109), specifier (D110), effect (D111) present:false - unmeasured, though the doubling 'hate and abhor' itself signals depth. Prohibition (D113) absent. The discovery note (D114) reads taab as abhorrence joined to hatred of falsehood. Role (D115) characteristic; locus (D116) internal:ib-state. The inner-being finding: here the interior's stance toward deceit is visceral loathing - not fear of it, not use of it, but disgust - and it is inseparable from love of the truth. To love God's law is to abhor the lie; the two affections are one movement of a heart aligned with truth.
narratives.story: In the closing stretch of the long psalm, the writer names his gut reaction to falsehood: 'I hate and abhor it - but I love your law.' This is not fear of the lie or clever use of it, but sheer disgust; falsehood turns his stomach. And it is bound tightly to its opposite: the very same heart that loathes the lie loves the truth of God's word, the two feelings being two sides of one loyalty. The passage does not measure the loathing or explain where it came from, though saying 'hate and abhor' together shows how deep it runs.
